questions.q: What does a compliance score represent?
options: The number of employees trained on security
The percentage of checks passed against one specific chosen benchmark
The uptime of a cloud resource
A universal security grade comparable across all benchmarks
questions.explain: A compliance score is checks passed divided by checks in the benchmark, and is only meaningful relative to that specific benchmark.

questions.q: In the remediation workflow described in this lesson, what happens immediately after a finding is surfaced?
options: It is assigned to the team or owner who can act on it
It is immediately deleted from the environment
It is automatically published publicly
It is ignored until the next audit
questions.explain: The workflow is surface, assign, fix, re-scan -- a finding nobody owns never gets fixed, so assignment comes right after surfacing.

questions.q: What is the difference between auto-remediation and a manual fix?
options: Auto-remediation applies a pre-approved scripted fix with no human step; a manual fix involves a person making a judgment-based change
Auto-remediation requires executive approval every time
Manual fixes are always faster than automation
They are the same thing with different names
questions.explain: Auto-remediation suits clear-cut cases with no judgment call; manual fixes suit cases that genuinely need human judgment.

questions.q: Why is re-scanning after remediation an important step?
options: It automatically raises the compliance score regardless of the fix
It is only needed once per year
It replaces the need for assigning a finding
It confirms the finding was actually resolved, not just marked resolved
questions.explain: Re-scanning turns 'we think we fixed it' into a confirmed result, which is why it's the final step in the workflow.

questions.q: Why can't a CIS Benchmark compliance score and a PCI DSS compliance score be directly compared?
options: They measure against different sets of checks/benchmarks
CIS Benchmark doesn't produce a numeric score
PCI DSS scores are always higher
They always produce identical results
questions.explain: Each score is only meaningful relative to the specific benchmark's checklist it was measured against.
